summary:
New Mexico sits inside the United States framework, which governs passports, visas, entry screening and federal facilities; the state's own law is among the most protective in the country for transgender people. A July 2026 national legal-risk ranking, compiled by applying a rubric to thousands of tracked anti-trans bills covering youth care, bathroom access, birth-certificate and driver's-licence restrictions and the withdrawal of legal recognition, placed New Mexico in a fifteen-jurisdiction "most protective" tier.

State law has prohibited discrimination on the basis of gender identity in employment, housing, credit, public accommodations and union membership since 1 July 2003. The exemption for employers with fewer than fifteen employees was repealed effective 1 July 2019, legislation passed in 2023 extended coverage explicitly to local entities, counties, schools, universities and government-run agencies under an emergency clause, and Albuquerque aligned its Human Rights Ordinance with the state scheme in May 2024.

Violence committed on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity has been covered by the state hate-crime law since 2003, and the common-law gay and trans panic defence was repealed by HB68, signed on 9 March 2022. School-bullying legislation passed in March 2019 and effective 1 July 2019 requires districts to protect students on the basis of gender identity, with policies covering prohibition, reporting, investigation, discipline, prevention and staff training.

No statewide measure restricts trans people's use of sex-segregated facilities, and since 1 July 2019 single-occupancy restrooms in businesses and public facilities must be marked gender-neutral and be available to any person regardless of gender identity or sex.

Since 1 November 2019, trans people may change their legal gender without surgery. The legislation repealed a 1984 surgery requirement and provides male, female and X designations on birth certificates, driver's licences and state identification. A birth-certificate change requires a completed Request to Change Gender Designation on a Birth Certificate form and fees, with parental consent for minors; licences and state IDs require a Request for Sex Designation Change form filed with the Motor Vehicles Division. Those forms replaced an earlier requirement for a perjury statement from an institution or physician confirming surgical change plus a certified name-change order. State-issued documents carry no weight in federal passport and visa processing, which is set nationally.

Health care is protected by statute. HB7, adopted in March 2023, codified protection for gender-affirming care and sexual reassignment surgery for adults on request without restrictions, expressly including interstate travellers, and the state is recorded as holding a shield law or executive order dated 2023 by the MAP Transgender Healthcare Equality Map (data as of 27 September 2026). The shield protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges where care that is lawful in New Mexico was banned in the patient's home state, which is the provision that matters most to a visitor travelling from a ban state. Gender-affirming care for minors is not banned here and the state is described as a sanctuary for transgender young people travelling from states that prohibit it. In 2026 the state health care authority announced it would use state funds to maintain Medicaid coverage for gender-affirming care after a federal rule to exclude it.

No state law bars transgender girls from school sports. Eligibility is determined by the original or amended birth certificate, and the New Mexico Activities Association has issued no further guidance on the question.
tangentialFactors:
Before colonisation, several Indigenous nations in what is now New Mexico recognised gender roles beyond the binary. The Navajo recognised four, including nadleehi, a male-bodied person with a feminine nature who was often chosen for roles such as spiritual healer and who traditionally wore women's clothes and did women's work; sexual relations with men were accepted. Comparable roles are recorded among the Zuni, including lhamana and katsotse, and among the Mescalero Apache, Tiwa, Tewa and the pueblos. Christian converts among the Hopi were at one point barred from the traditional snake dance because male cross-dressing could be observed, and Will Roscoe is documented as writing that reported tolerance or respect for transgender people fed historic-era explorers' argument for conquest in the name of Christianity.

Contemporary acceptance varies by community. LGBTQ Navajo may find acceptance within their families difficult, and 70% of LGBT Navajo youth are reported to have attempted suicide, a figure given without a denominator or methodology and therefore not usable as a measured rate.

Statewide polling found 73% support for anti-discrimination legislation protecting LGBTQ people in 2018, and 64% support in 2017 for a law covering sexual orientation and gender identity. Santa Fe is cited as a gay capital and Albuquerque, including its metropolitan area, as a gay-friendly city.

Consensual same-sex sexual activity has been legal since the anti-sodomy law was repealed in 1975; an attempt to reinstate it in 1986 failed. In 2013 the New Mexico Supreme Court unanimously upheld enforcement of the state non-discrimination law against a photographer who refused to photograph a same-sex commitment ceremony (Elane Photography v. Willock).
localsOnly:
Marriage rights are equal. The state Supreme Court required equal marriage rights on 19 December 2013, making New Mexico the seventeenth state to recognise it, and the legislature codified the position in March 2019 by votes of 62-0 in the House and 39-0 in the Senate; the governor signed it in April and it took effect on 1 July 2019. Partners of state employees have had access to benefits since 2003.

Single persons and same-sex couples may adopt, and second-parent adoptions are permitted with no statutory prohibition. Lesbian couples may access in vitro fertilisation and donor insemination regardless of sexual orientation or marital status, and the non-genetic, non-gestational mother is recognised as a legal parent. No statute or case law prohibits gestational or traditional surrogacy, which courts generally recognise.

Sexual orientation change efforts on minors are prohibited under SB121, passed 32-6 in the Senate and 44-23 in the House, signed by Governor Susana Martinez on 7 April 2017 and effective 6 July 2017.

HB31, adopted in 2023, repealed the requirement to publish a legal name change in a newspaper, a rule that had exposed transgender people's privacy and safety.

Discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation in employment, housing, credit, public accommodations and union membership has been prohibited since 1 July 2003, supplemented by a 1985 executive order barring sexual-orientation discrimination in public employment. The hate-crime law has covered violence based on actual or perceived sexual orientation since 2003, and the 2019 school-bullying legislation covers sexual orientation as well as gender identity.
outOfScopeNotes:
The July 2026 tier placement rests on a rubric applied to tracked legislation. It describes statutory posture rather than how the law is enforced in practice, and no enforcement data for the state's non-discrimination or hate-crime provisions was located.

The source inventory contains no New Mexico-specific record of anti-trans violence, arrests or prosecutions. No state-level violence rate can be stated, and the national picture governs that question.

The 2026 announcement that the state health care authority would fund Medicaid coverage for gender-affirming care after a federal exclusion rule does not state whether the funding is in operation.

The reported figure that 70% of LGBT Navajo youth have attempted suicide is given without a denominator, methodology or source and cannot be read as a measured rate.

Whether the New Mexico Activities Association will issue guidance on transgender students' sports eligibility, and how school districts will apply a birth-certificate standard, is unresolved.
